en.statement: Cloud agility helps teams turn new business ideas into working applications quickly.
en.explanation: On-demand resources shorten the wait for infrastructure, so teams can experiment and deliver new applications sooner.

en.statement: Horizontal scaling increases capacity by making an existing server more powerful.
en.explanation: Horizontal scaling adds resources, such as more servers, to share a workload instead of enlarging one server.

en.statement: Cloud elasticity matches available computing capacity to changes in workload demand.
en.explanation: Elastic capacity follows demand in both directions, helping workloads avoid keeping resources they no longer need.

en.statement: Deploying an application closer to its users can reduce the network latency they experience.
en.explanation: AWS offers deployment locations around the world, allowing applications to serve users from geographically closer infrastructure.

en.statement: High availability describes a workload's resistance to permanent loss of stored data.
en.explanation: Availability measures the proportion of time a workload is usable, expressed as uptime relative to the total time measured.

en.statement: Fault tolerance describes a workload's ability to operate despite a component failure.
en.explanation: Fault-tolerant workloads use redundant components that can take over the work of a failed component.

en.statement: Amazon RDS reduces database administration work by managing common maintenance tasks.
en.explanation: Amazon RDS handles routine tasks such as database software patching, freeing teams to focus on their applications.

source.title: What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?

en.statement: Launching an Amazon EC2 instance in one AWS Region creates copies in other Regions.
en.explanation: An Amazon EC2 instance belongs to its selected Region. Running copies elsewhere requires explicitly deploying them in those Regions.

en.statement: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling distributes incoming application requests among running instances.
en.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling manages instance capacity. Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming requests among instances.

source.title: Auto Scaling benefits for application architecture

en.statement: A highly available application requires deployment across multiple AWS Regions.
en.explanation: A workload can achieve high availability across multiple Availability Zones within one AWS Region.

source.title: Auto Scaling benefits for application architecture

en.statement: Infrastructure as a Service gives customers more system-level control than Software as a Service.
en.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service exposes infrastructure building blocks for customers to manage; Software as a Service provides a product managed by its provider.

en.statement: The reliability pillar's primary goal is the efficient use of computing resources.
en.explanation: Performance efficiency focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet a workload's performance requirements.

en.statement: Encrypting sensitive data supports the security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
en.explanation: The security pillar recommends protecting data with encryption, including data being stored and data being transmitted.

en.statement: Automatically recovering from failure is a design principle of the performance efficiency pillar.
en.explanation: Automatically recovering from failure is a reliability design principle, alongside testing recovery procedures and scaling horizontally.

en.statement: The sustainability pillar addresses the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads.
en.explanation: Sustainability considers energy use and resource efficiency to reduce a workload's environmental impact.

en.statement: The operational excellence pillar encourages teams to learn from day-to-day operations.
en.explanation: Teams improve operations by learning from operational events and metrics, then sharing those lessons across the organization.

en.statement: The AWS Well-Architected Framework recommends testing workloads at production scale.
en.explanation: On-demand infrastructure lets teams reproduce a production-sized test environment and remove it when testing finishes.

en.statement: The performance efficiency pillar evaluates the financial value of cloud spending.
en.explanation: Cost optimization focuses on delivering business value at the lowest price; performance efficiency focuses on effective use of computing resources.

en.statement: The operational excellence pillar favors frequent changes that are small and reversible.
en.explanation: Small, reversible changes reduce the impact of a failed change and make it easier to return to a working state.

en.statement: The security pillar treats perimeter protection as a substitute for layered security controls.
en.explanation: The security pillar recommends defense in depth: security controls at multiple layers, including networks, applications, and data.

en.statement: An AWS Well-Architected review is a compliance audit of an application's architecture.
en.explanation: A Well-Architected review is a constructive discussion that identifies architectural risks and opportunities to improve a workload.

en.statement: The AWS Well-Architected Framework supports evolving architecture as business needs change.
en.explanation: Cloud architectures can evolve as requirements change, rather than being fixed by an early design decision.

en.statement: The AWS Well-Architected Framework puts cost optimization ahead of reliability in pillar tradeoffs.
en.explanation: Pillar tradeoffs depend on business needs; a mission-critical workload can justify higher costs to improve reliability.

en.statement: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework helps organizations assess their readiness for cloud adoption.
en.explanation: It draws on AWS experience and best practices, and organizations also use it to prioritize transformation opportunities and to evolve a transformation roadmap.

source.title: An Overview of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework

en.statement: The AWS CAF People perspective focuses on designing the organization's cloud infrastructure.
en.explanation: In AWS CAF, People addresses culture, leadership, workforce, and organizational change; Platform addresses the cloud platform.

en.statement: The AWS CAF Governance perspective primarily handles the day-to-day delivery of cloud services.
en.explanation: In AWS CAF, Operations addresses ongoing service delivery; Governance coordinates cloud initiatives to maximize value and reduce transformation risks.

en.statement: The AWS CAF Business perspective connects cloud investments to the organization's business outcomes.
en.explanation: The AWS CAF Business perspective involves leaders such as the chief executive and chief financial officers, who align cloud investment with business goals.

en.statement: Rehosting moves an application to AWS while preserving its existing application architecture.
en.explanation: Rehosting transfers an application to cloud infrastructure with minimal application changes, making it a lift-and-shift approach.

en.statement: Replatforming requires redesigning an application's core architecture for the cloud.
en.explanation: Replatforming introduces cloud optimizations, such as using a managed database; redesigning the core architecture is refactoring.

en.statement: Repurchasing replaces an existing application with another product, such as a SaaS offering.
en.explanation: Repurchasing switches products instead of moving the existing application, for example by adopting a vendor-hosted software service.

en.statement: Retiring an application means keeping it in its current environment for later review.
en.explanation: Retiring decommissions an application; retaining keeps it in its current environment.

en.statement: An organization can choose different migration strategies for applications in the same portfolio.
en.explanation: Portfolio assessment assigns a migration approach to individual applications, reflecting their circumstances and business value.

source.title: Best practices for assessing applications to be retired during a migration to the AWS Cloud

en.statement: AWS Database Migration Service supports ongoing replication of changes during a data migration.
en.explanation: AWS Database Migration Service can copy existing data and replicate subsequent changes to keep the source and target synchronized.

source.title: What is AWS Database Migration Service?

en.statement: Migration Evaluator supports database replication when moving applications into the AWS Cloud.
en.explanation: Migration Evaluator assesses an existing environment to build a data-driven business case and cost estimates for migration.

en.statement: The AWS CAF Align phase focuses on expanding successful production pilots across the business.
en.explanation: In AWS CAF, Scale expands production pilots; Align identifies capability gaps, dependencies, and stakeholder concerns.

en.statement: The base compute charge for an Amazon EC2 On-Demand instance depends on its CPU utilization.
en.explanation: The base On-Demand compute charge for an Amazon EC2 instance accrues for its running time, including time when the instance is idle.

en.statement: Pay-as-you-go cloud computing replaces upfront infrastructure investment with usage-based expense.
en.explanation: Cloud consumption shifts spending from buying infrastructure in advance to paying for resources as they are used.

en.statement: The Amazon EC2 instance with the lowest hourly price provides the lowest total compute cost for a job.
en.explanation: Total compute cost depends on price and runtime; a higher-priced instance can cost less overall if it finishes a job sufficiently faster.

en.statement: Rightsizing reduces cloud costs by committing to a discounted resource usage rate.
en.explanation: Rightsizing matches resources to workload needs, such as reducing oversized Amazon EC2 instances; usage commitments are a separate savings approach.

source.title: Optimizing your cost with rightsizing recommendations

en.statement: AWS achieves economies of scale by aggregating infrastructure demand across many customers.
en.explanation: Combining demand lets AWS operate infrastructure at greater scale, which can lower the cost of providing resources.

en.statement: Bring Your Own License bundles the software license charge into the AWS service price.
en.explanation: Bring Your Own License uses eligible licenses supplied by the customer; license-included pricing bundles the software license with the service.

en.statement: AWS tiered volume pricing bases discounts on a customer's commitment to future usage.
en.explanation: Tiered volume discounts lower unit prices as eligible consumption grows; commitment discounts are a separate pricing mechanism.

en.statement: Using an existing software license on AWS depends on the software vendor's licensing terms.
en.explanation: Bring Your Own License requires checking the vendor's terms to confirm that the planned cloud deployment is permitted.

en.statement: After a workload migrates, cloud financial management becomes AWS's responsibility.
en.explanation: Customers need their own cloud financial management capability to track spending, allocate costs, and optimize business value.

en.statement: AWS cost optimization guidance recommends measuring a workload's business output alongside its cost.
en.explanation: The "measure overall efficiency" design principle ties spending to business output, so teams can see the gains from increasing output and reducing cost.

en.statement: AWS manages physical security at its data centers.
en.explanation: AWS protects the physical facilities that host its cloud infrastructure. Customers inherit these physical security controls.

en.statement: Customers maintain the hypervisor that supports Amazon EC2 virtual machines.
en.explanation: AWS maintains the underlying virtualization layer for Amazon EC2. Customer administration starts above that layer.

en.statement: Customers manage access permissions for their Amazon S3 objects.
en.explanation: Customers decide who can access their Amazon S3 data and configure permissions to enforce those decisions.

en.statement: In the shared responsibility model, security "of" the cloud is the customer's responsibility.
en.explanation: Security of the cloud is the AWS side of the model. The customer side is security in the cloud.

en.statement: A customer's security responsibilities vary with the AWS services they choose.
en.explanation: AWS services expose different levels of customer control. Choosing a more managed service shifts more infrastructure operation to AWS.

en.statement: Choosing the access rules for a customer's Amazon EC2 security groups is AWS's responsibility.
en.explanation: Customers configure Amazon EC2 security groups for their application's network access needs. AWS operates the underlying infrastructure.

en.statement: Customers control database-user access to their Amazon RDS databases.
en.explanation: Customers use their database engine's security features to manage database logins and permissions in Amazon RDS.

en.statement: Customers patch the operating systems that run the Amazon DynamoDB service.
en.explanation: AWS operates and maintains the infrastructure and operating systems behind Amazon DynamoDB. Customers remain responsible for their data.

en.statement: AWS provides security updates for supported AWS Lambda managed runtimes.
en.explanation: Lambda curates and publishes these patches and, by default, applies them to functions automatically. That responsibility ends when the runtime is deprecated.

en.statement: AWS patches third-party libraries that customers bundle with AWS Lambda function code.
en.explanation: Customers update libraries bundled with their AWS Lambda functions. Runtime security updates from AWS do not replace those application dependencies.

en.statement: Security awareness training is a shared control in the AWS shared responsibility model.
en.explanation: AWS trains its employees, while customers train theirs. Each organization implements security awareness training for its own staff.

en.statement: Configuration management is an inherited control in the AWS shared responsibility model.
en.explanation: Configuration management is a shared control: AWS configures its infrastructure, while customers configure their own systems.

en.statement: AWS Artifact provides AWS compliance reports for download.
en.explanation: AWS Artifact supplies reports and certifications that document AWS security controls. Customers can use these materials as evidence during audits.

en.statement: Encryption at rest refers to protecting data during network transmission.
en.explanation: Encryption at rest protects stored data, such as database records or files. Encryption in transit protects data exchanged between systems.

en.statement: AWS CloudTrail records AWS account activity for auditing.
en.explanation: AWS CloudTrail events document account activity, including actions performed through the console and APIs. Event details help investigators identify who performed an action and when.

en.statement: Using a PCI DSS compliant AWS service makes a customer's application PCI DSS compliant.
en.explanation: AWS PCI DSS compliance covers AWS's assessed environment. Customers must still meet the PCI DSS requirements that apply to their applications and validate their own compliance.

en.statement: Amazon CloudWatch Logs centralizes logs from applications and AWS services.
en.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch Logs collects and stores logs in a central service. Teams can search those logs to investigate operational or security issues.

en.statement: AWS compliance program coverage can differ between AWS services.
en.explanation: AWS publishes which services are in scope for each compliance program. Customers should check the relevant program before selecting services for regulated workloads.

source.title: AWS Services in Scope by Compliance Program

en.statement: AWS Config rules can block noncompliant resources from being created.
en.explanation: AWS Config evaluates resource configurations and flags noncompliant resources. Blocking an action takes a preventive control, such as an IAM policy.

source.title: Components of an AWS Config Rule

en.statement: AWS Key Management Service uses key policies to control access to KMS keys.
en.explanation: A key policy defines access controls for an AWS Key Management Service key. These controls help determine which identities can use or administer that key.

en.statement: Amazon GuardDuty filters network packets as an inline firewall.
en.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty detects suspicious activity and produces security findings. Inline packet filtering is a firewall function, not GuardDuty's threat-detection role.

en.statement: AWS Security Hub CSPM combines security findings from multiple AWS security services.
en.explanation: AWS Security Hub CSPM brings together findings from services such as Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Inspector. A consolidated view helps teams prioritize security issues.

source.title: Introduction to AWS Security Hub CSPM

en.statement: Amazon VPC Flow Logs capture the payloads of network packets.
en.explanation: VPC Flow Logs record traffic metadata, such as addresses and ports, rather than packet contents. Amazon VPC Traffic Mirroring supports inspection of actual packets.

en.statement: Least privilege limits an identity's permissions to what its tasks require.
en.explanation: Least privilege grants the access needed for a task and removes unnecessary permissions. This reduces the damage that mistakes or compromised credentials can cause.

en.statement: AWS recommends the root user for routine account administration.
en.explanation: AWS recommends using an administrative identity for routine work and reserving root access for tasks that require it. Root credentials need especially strong protection.

source.title: Root user best practices for your AWS account

en.statement: Multi-factor authentication adds an extra verification factor to AWS sign-in.
en.explanation: Multi-factor authentication combines different authentication factors, such as a password and a security device. A stolen password alone is then insufficient for that protected sign-in.

en.statement: An IAM user group provides a shared sign-in identity for its members.
en.explanation: An IAM user group organizes permissions for its members. Members authenticate using their own identities, rather than signing in as the group.

en.statement: Assuming an IAM role provides temporary security credentials.
en.explanation: An IAM role session uses temporary security credentials that expire. Roles let trusted users or workloads obtain access for that session.

en.statement: An IAM role's permissions policy identifies the principals trusted to assume that role.
en.explanation: An IAM role's trust policy identifies who can assume it. Its permissions policies define what actions a session using the role can perform.

en.statement: AWS IAM Identity Center supports workforce sign-in across multiple AWS accounts.
en.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center centralizes workforce access to assigned accounts and applications. It can use an existing identity provider or its own directory.

en.statement: IAM access keys are the credentials for AWS Management Console sign-in.
en.explanation: IAM access keys sign programmatic AWS requests. Direct IAM user sign-in to the AWS Management Console uses a username and password instead.

source.title: Manage access keys for IAM users

en.statement: AWS Secrets Manager rotates database credentials automatically on a schedule you configure.
en.explanation: With rotation configured, AWS Secrets Manager can update a stored database secret and the corresponding database credentials. Applications retrieve the updated secret when needed.

en.statement: An AWS Organizations service control policy grants permissions to IAM users.
en.explanation: A service control policy sets limits on available permissions. Access must still be granted through an applicable IAM or resource policy.

en.statement: Customer managed IAM policies can be reused across multiple identities in the same AWS account.
en.explanation: A customer managed IAM policy is a standalone policy that can be attached to multiple users, groups, or roles. Reusing it helps maintain consistent permissions.

en.statement: An IAM password policy sets expiration dates for IAM access keys.
en.explanation: An IAM password policy governs IAM user passwords. Password expiration does not expire an IAM user's access keys.

source.title: Set an account password policy for IAM users

en.statement: AWS WAF filters HTTP and HTTPS requests to protected web applications.
en.explanation: AWS WAF evaluates web requests against configured rules. Rules can help block requests that match threats such as SQL injection attempts.

en.statement: AWS Shield helps find software vulnerabilities by scanning Amazon EC2 instances.
en.explanation: AWS Shield protects against distributed denial-of-service attacks. Amazon Inspector is the AWS service that scans supported Amazon EC2 workloads for software vulnerabilities.

en.statement: AWS Marketplace includes third-party security products.
en.explanation: AWS Marketplace is a catalog for finding and obtaining third-party solutions. Its security offerings can complement native AWS security services.

en.statement: Amazon Inspector patches Amazon EC2 operating systems as part of a vulnerability scan.
en.explanation: Amazon Inspector identifies vulnerabilities and provides remediation guidance. Customers apply fixes, after which Inspector can detect the remediation and close the finding.

en.statement: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in Amazon S3 objects.
en.explanation: Amazon Macie analyzes Amazon S3 data to identify sensitive information, such as personal or financial data. Findings help teams locate data that needs protection.

en.statement: AWS Firewall Manager centrally manages security policies across accounts in AWS Organizations.
en.explanation: AWS Firewall Manager applies centrally defined protections across in-scope accounts and resources. This helps keep security policies consistent as an organization grows.

en.statement: AWS Security Bulletins provide personalized findings about resources in your AWS account.
en.explanation: AWS Security Bulletins publish notices about vulnerabilities affecting AWS services, software, and products. They are public advisories rather than an account-specific findings dashboard.

en.statement: AWS Certificate Manager manages access keys used to sign AWS API requests.
en.explanation: AWS Certificate Manager manages SSL/TLS certificates used to protect websites and applications. IAM manages the access keys used for programmatic AWS requests.

en.statement: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules in the AWS Cloud.
en.explanation: AWS CloudHSM supplies single-tenant hardware security modules for cryptographic operations. Customers control the keys and users within their HSMs.

en.statement: A security group in Amazon VPC can contain explicit deny rules.
en.explanation: Amazon VPC security group rules allow specified traffic; they do not provide explicit deny rules. Network ACLs support both allow and deny rules.

en.statement: AWS Trusted Advisor security checks identify risky resource configurations.
en.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor includes security checks for issues such as overly permissive security groups. Its recommendations help teams review and improve their configurations.

source.title: Security checks in AWS Trusted Advisor

en.statement: Network ACLs in Amazon VPC support stateful filtering that allows response traffic.
en.explanation: Amazon VPC network ACLs are stateless, so return traffic must be permitted by their rules. Security groups track connection state instead.

source.title: Control subnet traffic with network access control lists

en.statement: The AWS Management Console provides a web interface for managing AWS resources.
en.explanation: The AWS Management Console brings service management into a browser. Its visual interface supports interactive tasks such as inspecting and creating resources.

source.title: What is the AWS Management Console?

en.statement: Developers write shell scripts that run AWS CLI commands to manage their AWS resources.
en.explanation: The AWS CLI gives direct access to the public APIs of AWS services from a command-line shell, so a script can repeat the same resource-management steps each time it runs.

source.title: What is the AWS Command Line Interface?

en.statement: AWS CloudFormation uses the term stack for an individual virtual machine.
en.explanation: An AWS CloudFormation stack is a collection of AWS resources managed as one unit. A stack can include resources such as servers and databases.

source.title: Managing AWS resources as a single unit with CloudFormation stacks

en.statement: A hybrid cloud deployment is defined by using multiple public cloud providers.
en.explanation: Hybrid cloud connects an organization's own infrastructure with public cloud services. Using multiple cloud providers describes multicloud.

en.statement: AWS SDKs provide language-specific libraries for applications to interact with AWS services.
en.explanation: AWS SDKs let developers use AWS service APIs from application code. The libraries handle connection details such as request signing and retries.

en.statement: An on-premises deployment that uses virtualization provides most of the benefits of cloud computing.
en.explanation: AWS says on-premises deployment with virtualization, sometimes called private cloud, lacks many of the benefits of cloud computing and is mostly the same as legacy IT.

source.title: Types of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services

en.statement: AWS CloudFormation templates allow infrastructure definitions to be tracked in version control.
en.explanation: AWS CloudFormation templates express infrastructure as text. Version control can show how the definitions change and who makes those changes.

en.statement: AWS Outposts runs customer workloads on computing hardware inside an AWS regional data center.
en.explanation: AWS Outposts brings AWS-owned, AWS-managed infrastructure to a customer's premises. It extends AWS services to the customer's location.

en.statement: AWS CloudFormation templates specify the exact sequence of commands used to provision resources.
en.explanation: AWS CloudFormation templates describe the desired resources. CloudFormation handles their provisioning and dependencies, rather than requiring an ordered command script.

en.statement: A cloud deployment can host applications that originate in an on-premises environment.
en.explanation: Cloud-hosted applications can be migrated from existing environments or built for the cloud. An application's original location does not determine its current deployment model.

en.statement: AWS Service Catalog is a public marketplace for buying third-party software.
en.explanation: AWS Service Catalog organizes IT services approved by an organization. End users can provision those approved offerings within organizational controls.

en.statement: AWS Elastic Beanstalk provisions infrastructure for the application code a customer deploys.
en.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk creates the resources needed to run a deployed application. It handles infrastructure tasks so developers can focus on their code.

en.statement: An Availability Zone extends across multiple AWS Regions.
en.explanation: An Availability Zone is an isolated location within an AWS Region. The Region contains the Availability Zones, rather than the other way around.

en.statement: An AWS Region is a separate geographic area containing AWS infrastructure.
en.explanation: AWS groups infrastructure into geographic Regions. Choosing a Region determines the geographic location of the regional resources you deploy.

en.statement: An Availability Zone is made up of one or more discrete data centers.
en.explanation: AWS defines an Availability Zone as one or more data centers in a Region. An Availability Zone is an infrastructure grouping, not necessarily a single building.

en.statement: Availability Zones in an AWS Region depend on a shared power supply.
en.explanation: Availability Zones have independent power infrastructure. This separation helps isolate failures between zones in the same Region.

en.statement: Distributing an application across Availability Zones improves resilience to a zone failure.
en.explanation: A multi-AZ application can continue using resources in healthy zones when a zone fails. The application must be designed to use that redundancy.

en.statement: AWS connects Availability Zones within a Region through the public internet.
en.explanation: AWS interconnects Availability Zones with redundant, dedicated network links. These links support high-bandwidth, low-latency communication within a Region.

en.statement: Requirements about where data resides influence the choice of an AWS Region.
en.explanation: An AWS Region places regional resources in a particular geographic location. Data residency and regulatory requirements can therefore guide Region selection.

en.statement: Deploying a recovery environment in another AWS Region supports recovery from a regional outage.
en.explanation: A separate Region provides a recovery location outside the affected Region. Disaster recovery requires preparing the needed application resources and data.

source.title: REL10-BP01 Deploy the workload to multiple locations

en.statement: Amazon CloudFront routes a viewer's request to the edge location nearest the content's origin.
en.explanation: Amazon CloudFront routes a viewer's request to an edge location that provides low latency to that viewer. Proximity to the origin is not the routing goal.

en.statement: Amazon EC2 provides virtual servers for running applications in the cloud.
en.explanation: With Amazon EC2, customers launch instances to host their workloads. Instance types provide different combinations of processing, memory, and storage.

en.statement: Amazon ECS provides managed Kubernetes clusters for containerized applications.
en.explanation: Amazon EKS is the AWS service for managed Kubernetes. Kubernetes provides the orchestration for applications running in its clusters.

en.statement: Amazon ECR schedules application containers to run across a cluster.
en.explanation: Amazon ECR stores and manages container images. A container platform retrieves those images to run the applications they contain.

source.title: What is Amazon Elastic Container Registry?

en.statement: AWS Lambda is a compute service that runs application functions in response to events.
en.explanation: AWS Lambda executes function code when it is invoked. Event-driven applications use this model to run processing when work arrives.

en.statement: AWS Fargate provides serverless compute capacity for running containers.
en.explanation: AWS Fargate runs containers while AWS manages the underlying servers. Customers focus on the containerized workload rather than operating its server fleet.

source.title: Architect for AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS

en.statement: Compute optimized Amazon EC2 instances suit applications that require intensive CPU processing.
en.explanation: Compute optimized Amazon EC2 instances emphasize processor performance. They fit workloads such as scientific calculations and media processing.

source.title: Specifications for Amazon EC2 compute optimized instances

en.statement: Storage optimized Amazon EC2 instances target CPU-intensive calculations.
en.explanation: Storage optimized Amazon EC2 instances focus on demanding local-storage access. They suit workloads that need fast reads and writes over large datasets.

source.title: Specifications for Amazon EC2 storage optimized instances

en.statement: Elastic Load Balancing launches additional application servers as incoming demand increases.
en.explanation: Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming traffic among targets. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can add instances when an application needs more computing capacity.

en.statement: Workloads that process large datasets in memory are the target of memory optimized Amazon EC2 instances.
en.explanation: Memory optimized Amazon EC2 instances are designed for memory-intensive processing. They help applications work efficiently with large datasets held in RAM.

source.title: Specifications for Amazon EC2 memory optimized instances

en.statement: AWS Batch deploys customer-facing web applications.
en.explanation: AWS Batch schedules and runs batch computing jobs, such as simulations or data processing. It provisions computing resources for the submitted work.

en.statement: Amazon Aurora stores data as NoSQL key-value items.
en.explanation: Amazon Aurora is a managed relational database engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL. It belongs to the relational database category.

en.statement: Amazon DynamoDB supports a key-value data model for NoSQL applications.
en.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database supporting key-value and document data. AWS handles the database infrastructure so developers can focus on applications.

en.statement: Amazon ElastiCache is a relational database service for SQL transactions.
en.explanation: Amazon ElastiCache provides a managed in-memory data store or cache. Its role is fast data access, rather than operating a relational SQL database.

en.statement: Amazon Neptune suits applications that query relationships in highly connected data.
en.explanation: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database. Its graph model supports relationship-heavy use cases such as fraud detection and recommendation engines.

en.statement: Amazon DocumentDB organizes application data as normalized relational tables.
en.explanation: Amazon DocumentDB uses a document data model. Documents let applications persist data in a structure similar to the objects they use in code.

en.statement: AWS patches the database software that a customer installs directly on Amazon EC2.
en.explanation: Customers manage and patch database software they install on Amazon EC2. AWS manages the underlying physical infrastructure.

source.title: What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?

en.statement: Running a self-managed database on Amazon EC2 gives customers control over the server operating system.
en.explanation: On EC2, AWS manages only the hardware layers. The customer installs and patches the operating system and database software, and a manual update might cause downtime.

source.title: What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?

en.statement: AWS Database Migration Service handles migrations between different database engines.
en.explanation: DMS supports fully heterogeneous migrations between its supported engines. The schema is converted first, with DMS Schema Conversion or AWS SCT, and DMS then moves the data.

source.title: What is AWS Database Migration Service?

en.statement: Amazon RDS makes AWS responsible for tuning the SQL queries written by an application team.
en.explanation: Customers are responsible for tuning their Amazon RDS queries. AWS manages the database infrastructure, while query performance depends on application-specific design.

source.title: What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?

en.statement: Amazon Redshift is optimized for recording individual sales transactions as customers place orders.
en.explanation: Amazon Redshift is designed for analytical queries over large datasets. Its data warehouse role differs from processing an application's individual sales transactions.

en.statement: AWS Schema Conversion Tool converts table definitions when a migration changes the database engine.
en.explanation: AWS Schema Conversion Tool translates database structures into a form suitable for the target engine. It also identifies structures that need manual conversion.

source.title: What is the AWS Schema Conversion Tool?

en.statement: An Amazon VPC is a logically isolated virtual network for AWS resources.
en.explanation: Amazon VPC lets you define a virtual network for your AWS resources. You control its address ranges, subnets, and routing.

en.statement: A subnet in Amazon VPC spans multiple Availability Zones.
en.explanation: An Amazon VPC subnet resides within one Availability Zone. Deploying across Availability Zones requires separate subnets.

en.statement: An internet gateway enables communication between an Amazon VPC and the internet.
en.explanation: An internet gateway provides internet connectivity for an Amazon VPC. Resources also need suitable addressing and routes to use that connection.

source.title: Enable internet access for a VPC using an internet gateway

en.statement: Amazon Route 53 is the service that routes traffic between subnets in an Amazon VPC.
en.explanation: Amazon Route 53 uses DNS to direct users to application endpoints. It resolves domain names rather than acting as a router between subnets.

en.statement: AWS Site-to-Site VPN provides encrypted tunnels between on-premises networks and AWS.
en.explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN links an on-premises network to AWS using IPsec tunnels. Encryption protects the traffic carried through those tunnels.

en.statement: AWS Direct Connect carries its connection to AWS over the public internet.
en.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a private network path to AWS that bypasses the public internet. It connects your network through a Direct Connect location.

en.statement: Amazon VPC route tables determine where network traffic is directed.
en.explanation: Amazon VPC route tables define paths for traffic from subnets or gateways. A route links a destination network to a target.

en.statement: A security group in Amazon VPC can apply its traffic rules to an entire subnet.
en.explanation: Security groups protect associated resources, such as Amazon EC2 instances. Network ACLs apply traffic filtering at the subnet boundary.

source.title: Ensure internetwork traffic privacy in Amazon VPC

en.statement: Amazon CloudFront caches web content at edge locations near viewers.
en.explanation: Amazon CloudFront serves cached content from edge locations to reduce delivery latency. An origin supplies content when the edge needs it.

en.statement: VPC endpoints provide private access from an Amazon VPC to supported AWS services.
en.explanation: VPC endpoints let resources reach supported AWS services privately. This access avoids the need for an internet gateway.

en.statement: VPC B and VPC C, both peered with VPC A, can route traffic to one another through VPC A.
en.explanation: VPC peering does not support transitive relationships, so VPC B and VPC C cannot route through VPC A. They need a peering connection of their own, or a transit gateway instead.

en.statement: Amazon S3 stores application data as objects organized within buckets.
en.explanation: Amazon S3 uses object storage: a bucket holds objects containing data and metadata. This suits uses such as media files and backups.

en.statement: Amazon EBS provides managed file storage for shared network folders.
en.explanation: Amazon EBS supplies block storage volumes for Amazon EC2. A volume behaves like an attached disk rather than a managed shared file system.

source.title: What is Amazon Elastic Block Store?

en.statement: Amazon EFS provides shared file storage accessible by multiple compute instances.
en.explanation: Amazon EFS provides a managed file system that multiple compute instances can access. Applications can work with shared files through the NFS protocol.

source.title: What is Amazon Elastic File System?

en.statement: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides file storage accessed over the SMB protocol.
en.explanation: The file servers are built on Microsoft Windows Server, with native support for Windows file system features, and users are authenticated with Microsoft Active Directory.

source.title: What is FSx for Windows File Server?

en.statement: Amazon EC2 instance store preserves its data after the instance is stopped.
en.explanation: Amazon EC2 instance store is temporary storage whose data is lost when the instance stops. Important data needs a persistent storage destination.

source.title: Data persistence for Amazon EC2 instance store volumes

en.statement: AWS Backup centralizes backup management across supported AWS services.
en.explanation: AWS Backup brings backup and recovery management into one service. Backup policies can protect supported resources such as volumes, databases, and file systems.

en.statement: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises applications with AWS cloud storage.
en.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway bridges on-premises environments and AWS storage. Its caching options keep frequently accessed data locally while using cloud storage.

en.statement: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive suits frequently accessed application data.
en.explanation: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive targets long-term archival data that is rarely accessed. A storage class intended for frequent access better fits active application data.

source.title: Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes

en.statement: Amazon S3 Lifecycle rules move stored objects between AWS Regions.
en.explanation: Amazon S3 Lifecycle rules transition objects between storage classes or expire them. Cross-Region Replication copies objects to a bucket in another Region.

en.statement: With S3 Intelligent-Tiering, customers move objects between the Frequent and Infrequent Access tiers by hand.
en.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects not accessed for 30 consecutive days to the Infrequent Access tier on its own. A restore is needed only for the opt-in Archive Access and Deep Archive Access tiers.

source.title: Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes

en.statement: Deleting an Amazon EBS volume also deletes its existing snapshots.
en.explanation: Amazon EBS snapshots persist independently of their source volume. Retained snapshots can restore data after the volume is deleted.

source.title: What is Amazon Elastic Block Store?

en.statement: Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is a storage class for rarely accessed data that needs immediate retrieval.
en.explanation: Unlike Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive, it needs no restore: objects are read in milliseconds. The trade-off is a 90-day minimum storage duration and per-GB retrieval fees.

source.title: Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes

en.statement: Amazon SageMaker AI provides managed training for custom machine learning models.
en.explanation: Amazon SageMaker AI manages infrastructure for training machine learning models. Developers can use their own algorithms and training data.

en.statement: Amazon Polly translates written text from one language into another.
en.explanation: Amazon Polly turns text into lifelike speech. Amazon Translate handles text translation between languages.

source.title: Choosing an AWS machine learning service

en.statement: Amazon Rekognition identifies objects that appear in digital images.
en.explanation: Amazon Rekognition uses machine learning to analyze visual content. Object detection can help label images without building a custom vision model.

en.statement: Amazon Textract identifies the sentiment expressed in written product reviews.
en.explanation: Amazon Textract extracts text and structured data from documents. Understanding the sentiment expressed in that text is a natural language processing task.

en.statement: Amazon Lex is a service for building conversational chatbots into applications.
en.explanation: Amazon Lex provides speech recognition and language understanding for voice or text chatbots. It manages the dialog between an application and a user.

en.statement: Amazon Comprehend converts recorded conversations into written transcripts.
en.explanation: Amazon Transcribe converts recorded speech into text. Amazon Comprehend analyzes text to extract insights about its content.

source.title: Choosing an AWS machine learning service

en.statement: Amazon Quick Sight creates interactive dashboards for business data analysis.
en.explanation: Amazon Quick Sight provides business intelligence through visualizations and dashboards. AWS currently presents it as a feature within Amazon Quick.

en.statement: Amazon Athena queries data stored in Amazon S3 using SQL.
en.explanation: Amazon Athena runs SQL queries directly against data in Amazon S3. AWS manages the query infrastructure, making it useful for interactive analysis.

en.statement: AWS Glue provides a managed data warehouse for running analytical queries.
en.explanation: AWS Glue is a data integration service for discovering, preparing, and combining data. Its extract, transform, and load capabilities prepare data for analytics.

en.statement: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams collects streaming data for real-time processing.
en.explanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams captures continuous data such as application logs and website activity. Applications can process that data as it arrives.

source.title: What is Amazon Kinesis Data Streams?

en.statement: Amazon EMR provides a managed search engine for querying indexed application logs.
en.explanation: Amazon EMR is a big data platform for distributed processing with frameworks such as Apache Spark and Hadoop. Its core role is running data-processing workloads.

en.statement: Amazon SQS is a managed message queue service that decouples application components.
en.explanation: Amazon SQS holds messages between producing and consuming components. Consumers can process queued work independently of when producers submit it.

source.title: What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?

en.statement: Amazon SNS load-balances a topic's notifications across its subscribers.
en.explanation: Amazon SNS can deliver a published message to multiple subscribed endpoints. Subscribers receive copies of a notification rather than competing for pooled work.

en.statement: Amazon EventBridge routes events from producers to consumer applications.
en.explanation: Amazon EventBridge connects applications through events. It can deliver events from AWS services, custom applications, and third-party software to consumers.

en.statement: Amazon SES provides a cloud contact center for customer service agents.
en.explanation: Amazon SES is an email service for application communications, such as order confirmations and newsletters. Its role is email delivery rather than operating a contact center.

en.statement: AWS Support offers plans that include technical assistance from AWS experts.
en.explanation: AWS Support plans can provide human technical assistance for AWS workloads. Available assistance depends on the support plan selected.

en.statement: AWS CodeBuild coordinates the stages of a continuous delivery pipeline.
en.explanation: AWS CodePipeline coordinates a delivery workflow. AWS CodeBuild handles build tasks such as compiling source code and running tests within that workflow.

en.statement: AWS X-Ray traces requests as they pass through distributed applications.
en.explanation: AWS X-Ray collects request traces across application components. These traces help reveal errors and performance bottlenecks.

en.statement: Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser provides cloud-hosted Windows desktops for remote work.
en.explanation: Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser provides remote browser sessions for websites and web applications. Its focus is secure browsing rather than a full Windows desktop.

en.statement: AWS Amplify provides managed hosting for frontend web applications.
en.explanation: AWS Amplify Hosting deploys web applications using a managed hosting service. It supports common frontend frameworks, helping teams publish their applications.

en.statement: AWS IoT Core executes application logic locally on connected devices.
en.explanation: AWS IoT Core provides cloud services that connect devices with AWS and exchange their messages. Local execution on a device is an edge-computing responsibility.

en.statement: Amazon WorkSpaces supplies cloud-based virtual desktops to end users.
en.explanation: Amazon WorkSpaces gives users access to hosted virtual desktops. Users can connect from supported devices instead of relying on a locally hosted desktop environment.

en.statement: AWS Step Functions provides an event bus that routes events between applications.
en.explanation: AWS Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows. It coordinates the progression of tasks rather than serving as an event bus.

en.statement: Amazon EC2 On-Demand pricing is a good fit for short-term workloads with unpredictable compute needs.
en.explanation: Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances let you pay for compute as you use it, without a long-term commitment. This suits short-lived or irregular workloads.

source.title: Purchasing On-Demand Instances for Amazon EC2

en.statement: Amazon EC2 Spot Instances provide spare compute capacity at a discount to On-Demand prices.
en.explanation: Amazon EC2 sells spare capacity as Spot Instances. AWS can reclaim that capacity, so Spot suits workloads that tolerate interruptions.

en.statement: Convertible Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances support exchanges for different instance types.
en.explanation: Convertible Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances can be exchanged for another eligible configuration. This provides flexibility when compute requirements change.

source.title: Reserved Instances for Amazon EC2 overview

en.statement: Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances provide an entire physical server for exclusive use.
en.explanation: An Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance is a billing discount applied to matching instance usage, rather than a physical server reserved for a customer.

source.title: Reserved Instances for Amazon EC2 overview

en.statement: Customers bring existing per-socket and per-core software licenses to Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts.
en.explanation: A Dedicated Host gives visibility of its server's sockets and physical cores, the units that per-socket and per-core licenses are bound to. The software license terms still apply.

en.statement: Amazon EC2 Dedicated Instances share physical host hardware with instances from other AWS accounts.
en.explanation: Amazon EC2 Dedicated Instances run on hardware isolated from other AWS accounts. They may share hardware with other instances from the same account.

en.statement: An Amazon EC2 On-Demand Capacity Reservation includes a discount on the reserved compute capacity.
en.explanation: Amazon EC2 On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve capacity, rather than discount it. Eligible Savings Plans or Regional Reserved Instances can provide a separate discount.

source.title: Reserve compute capacity with EC2 On-Demand Capacity Reservations

en.statement: AWS Organizations can share eligible Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance discounts across member accounts.
en.explanation: Consolidated billing supports sharing eligible Reserved Instance discounts across accounts in AWS Organizations. Discount sharing lets another account benefit from unused discounts.

en.statement: AWS Savings Plans base the customer's commitment on a fixed number of Amazon EC2 instances.
en.explanation: AWS Savings Plans use a spending commitment measured in dollars per hour. The commitment is a usage-spending amount, rather than a fixed instance count.

en.statement: Amazon EC2 includes cross-Region data transfer in its instance compute charges.
en.explanation: Amazon EC2 compute usage and cross-Region data transfer have separate pricing. Transferring data between Regions generally incurs data transfer charges.

en.statement: Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access includes data retrieval in its storage charge.
en.explanation: Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access has data retrieval charges in addition to storage charges. Retrieval costs matter when comparing storage classes.

en.statement: Standard internet uploads to Amazon S3 are free of data transfer charges.
en.explanation: Amazon S3 waives standard data transfer charges for data received from the internet. Storage, requests, and optional transfer acceleration can still incur charges.

en.statement: AWS Cost Explorer shows historical spending trends across AWS services.
en.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer visualizes cost and usage over time. Its graphs and reports help identify spending patterns and investigate cost changes.

source.title: Analyzing your costs and usage with AWS Cost Explorer

en.statement: The AWS Billing and Cost Management console provides access to downloadable AWS invoices.
en.explanation: The Bills page in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console provides invoices and charge details. Use it to review issued bills.

en.statement: AWS Budgets can alert you when forecast spending exceeds a configured cost threshold.
en.explanation: AWS Budgets supports alerts based on forecast costs. A forecast alert can warn you before actual spending reaches the configured threshold.

source.title: Managing your costs with AWS Budgets

en.statement: Setting an AWS Budgets cost budget creates an enforced spending cap for the account.
en.explanation: An AWS Budgets cost budget tracks spending rather than imposing a hard spending cap. Costs can exceed its threshold, even when alerts or budget actions are configured.

source.title: Managing your costs with AWS Budgets

en.statement: AWS Organizations combines eligible usage across accounts to qualify for volume discounts.
en.explanation: Consolidated billing combines eligible usage from accounts in AWS Organizations. Aggregated usage can qualify for volume discounts that smaller accounts would miss separately.

en.statement: AWS Organizations consolidated billing moves member-account resources into the management account.
en.explanation: Consolidated billing combines payment responsibilities while accounts remain separate. Resources remain in their own accounts with independent access permissions.

en.statement: Activated cost allocation tags help group AWS resource charges by project in billing reports.
en.explanation: Cost allocation tags organize AWS costs into business categories, such as projects. Activate the relevant tags so their values can appear in cost reports.

source.title: Organizing and tracking costs using AWS cost allocation tags

en.statement: AWS Cost and Usage Reports provide detailed records of AWS service usage and associated charges.
en.explanation: AWS Cost and Usage Reports contain detailed cost and usage data. These records support analysis beyond a high-level monthly bill.

source.title: What are AWS Cost and Usage Reports?

en.statement: AWS Organizations consolidated billing requires member accounts to pay AWS separately for their usage.
en.explanation: Consolidated billing centralizes payment instead of requiring separate member-account payments. A member account's cost breakdown is informational rather than a separate bill to pay.

en.statement: An AWS Pricing Calculator estimate is a binding quote for the planned AWS workload.
en.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates costs from your inputs; it does not provide a binding quote. Actual charges depend on actual usage and applicable pricing.

en.statement: An AWS Organizations member account sees other members' costs in AWS Cost Explorer by default.
en.explanation: By default, member accounts see their own costs in AWS Cost Explorer. The management account can view cost information across the organization.

en.statement: AWS Basic Support includes help with questions about an AWS account and its bill.
en.explanation: AWS customers can open account and billing support cases with Basic Support. This differs from technical troubleshooting cases, which require an eligible paid support plan.

en.statement: AWS Business Support+ includes a designated technical account manager for the customer.
en.explanation: AWS Enterprise Support includes a designated technical account manager. AWS Business Support+ does not include that designated role.

en.statement: AWS Support response-time targets specify when a reported technical issue is fully resolved.
en.explanation: AWS Support response-time targets concern the initial response to a case. They are not promises to resolve the issue within that time.

en.statement: AWS Trusted Advisor identifies opportunities to reduce spending on AWS resources.
en.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor includes checks for cost-saving opportunities in your AWS environment. Reviewing its recommendations can help identify inefficient resource use.

en.statement: AWS Health Dashboard shows AWS service events that can affect your AWS resources.
en.explanation: AWS Health Dashboard provides visibility into service health events and planned changes affecting your resources. This helps connect AWS events with potential workload impact.

en.statement: Reading community questions and answers on AWS re:Post depends on a paid AWS Support plan.
en.explanation: AWS re:Post community resources are available with Basic Support. A paid AWS Support plan is not required to consult community questions and answers.

en.statement: AWS Knowledge Center provides personalized status updates for a customer's open support cases.
en.explanation: AWS Knowledge Center provides answers to common troubleshooting questions. It is a self-service knowledge resource, rather than a system for tracking private support cases.

en.statement: AWS Prescriptive Guidance generates recommendations by scanning resources in your AWS account.
en.explanation: AWS Prescriptive Guidance provides expert-written guides and implementation patterns. Its guidance is published technical content, rather than findings from account scans.

en.statement: The AWS Partner Network supports participating companies in developing solutions for AWS customers.
en.explanation: The APN is a global community of organizations that use AWS technologies, programs, funding and tools to build solutions and services for customers.

source.title: Become an AWS Partner | AWS Partner Network

en.statement: AWS Professional Services provides expert assistance for projects that migrate workloads to AWS.
en.explanation: AWS Professional Services delivers consulting engagements for cloud transformation. Its experts help organizations plan and carry out migration projects.

en.statement: AWS Trust and Safety is the contact for routine billing questions about AWS service charges.
en.explanation: The AWS Trust and Safety team handles reports of abuse involving AWS resources. Its reporting role concerns misuse of the platform, rather than routine billing questions.

source.title: Content Domain 4: Billing, Pricing, and Support
